run.question: 配置的业务数据库里有哪些表？orders 表里每种 status 的订单各有多少条、failed 占比多少？请用数据库只读查询工具核实后回答。

report.summary: Read-only queries against the configured ClickHouse database (source otel-demo) show exactly one table, default.orders, with columns id (UInt32), customer (String), status (String) and amount (Decimal(10,2)), and sorting key id. Grouping default.orders by status returns three distinct values: paid 144, failed 72, refunded 24, total 240 rows; failed is therefore 72/240 = 0.30, i.e. 30% of all orders. These are point-in-time readings taken at about 2026-11-20T21:27:44-45Z (the database as it is now), not a historical view of the authorized window (2026-11-19T21:27:41Z to 2026-11-20T21:27:41Z), and no incident or health conclusion is drawn from them.

claims.text: The configured ClickHouse database contains one table, default.orders; it is listed as type table (no views were listed, and the listing was not truncated).
Table default.orders has four columns: id UInt32 (not nullable, primary/sorting key), customer String, status String, amount Decimal(10,2).
Grouping default.orders by status returns exactly three values: paid = 144 rows, failed = 72 rows, refunded = 24 rows (3 rows returned, none omitted or truncated).
Across default.orders there are 240 rows in total, of which 72 have status = 'failed', a failed ratio of 0.3 (30%), computed by the database in a single aggregation query.

All three database views were read at query time (observed about 2026-11-20T21:27:42-45Z) and state they describe the database as it is now, not its state during the authorized window ending 2026-11-20T21:27:41Z.

gaps: The table listing and status counts are current-state readings; there is no evidence of what the orders table contained during the authorized window, so no trend, change or incident-time statement about the orders data is supported.
The listing shows only what the configured read-only account and the single configured schema expose; tables invisible to that account or in schemas not listed remain unknown.
Whether the 30% failed ratio relates to any service error or incident is not investigated here and is not inferred.
next_steps: If the failure ratio needs to be tied to an incident, compare it with payment/checkout error signals (traces_span_metrics_calls_total status_code, rpc_grpc_status_code) over the authorized window rather than the current-state table snapshot.
If historical order status distributions are needed, arrange a time-series source of order status changes, since the orders table only holds current rows.
